PROPOSED EMPIRICAL RESEARCH PLAN  
(Everything that follows is what I would do given the data and institutional setting described.  I do NOT rely on any existing paper.)

────────────────────────────────────────
1. IDENTIFICATION STRATEGY
────────────────────────────────────────
I combine two complementary strategies.

A. Difference-in-Differences / Event Study (county panel 1790–2000)  
   • Goal: test whether the relative population advantage of portage sites survives once the original advantage is technologically neutralised (arrival of railroads / locks).  
   • Approach: compare population growth of “portage counties” to otherwise similar “river counties” before and after the county-specific year in which the river became navigable without trans-shipment (obsolescence date).  Estimate a two-way-fixed-effects (TWFE) event-study:  

        ln Pop_ct = Σ_{k≠-1} β_k (Portage_c × EventTime_{t=k}) + γ_c + δ_t + X_c′λ + ε_ct

B. Cross-sectional IV (tract level, year 2000)  
   • Goal: quantify the causal persistence mechanism.  
   • First stage: instrument 1790 (or 1850) population with the exogenous geologic dummy Portage_c.  
   • Second stage: regress 2000 population density (or nighttime-lights) on the predicted early-period population.  
   • Interpretation: β_IV >1 implies increasing returns; β_IV ≈1 implies persistence through sunk historical investment; β_IV <1 means mean-reversion.

────────────────────────────────────────
2. TREATMENT AND CONTROL
────────────────────────────────────────
A. DID / Event Study  
   • Treatment variable: Portage_c =1 if county centroid lies within 5 km of a historical portage point.  
   • Control group: counties whose major river touches the fall line but where no portage was required (or whose closest river segment became navigable naturally).  These “river counties” share river access and coastal proximity but lack the original trans-shipment advantage.  
   • Treatment timing: ObsolescenceYear_c = min{ year of first railroad connection within 10 km, year canal/lock completed that bypassed the fall }.  Event time k = t – ObsolescenceYear_c.  

B. IV  
   • Instrument: Portage_c as above.  
   • Endogenous regressor: ln Pop_c,1790 (or 1850).  
   • Outcome: ln Pop_c,2000, ln lights_c,2003.  
   • Controls X_c: elevation, climate, river navigability 1890, distance to coast, presence of aquifer, 1885 water-power potential, 1850 rail lines, seaport dummy, etc.

────────────────────────────────────────
3. KEY IDENTIFYING ASSUMPTIONS
────────────────────────────────────────
A. DID
   1. Parallel trends: absent the obsolescence shock, portage and control counties would have had parallel population paths.  
      – Plausible because both lie on the same rivers & fall line; pre-trend tests will be performed.  
   2. Stable composition: no systematic county boundary changes after my NHGIS harmonisation.  
   3. No spillovers: growth in a treated county does not mechanically depress a neighbouring control county.  I will cluster at the river-segment level and run spatial spillover tests.

B. IV
   1. Relevance: Portage status strongly predicts early population (commerce cluster); can be verified.  
   2. Exclusion: Portage has no direct effect on 2000 population except through its effect on early population.  Because portage is geologically defined and the shipping advantage is obsolete, this is plausible once I control for any remaining water-power potential and modern water amenities.  
   3. Monotonicity: Portage never reduced early population.

────────────────────────────────────────
4. THREATS TO IDENTIFICATION & REMEDIES
────────────────────────────────────────
1. Non-shipping advantages of waterfalls (hydro-power, scenery) could generate modern population directly.  
   → Control for 1885 water-power horsepower, present-day slope, 1900 manufacturing mix; re-estimate excluding hydro-power rich sites.  
2. Government siting of state capitals at fall-line towns (e.g., Richmond, Columbia) introduces political shocks.  
   → Add state-capital dummy; run robustness dropping capitals.  
3. Selective railroad routing: railroads may have endogenously connected already-growing portage towns, confounding the timing.  
   → Use instrumented railroad arrival dates (predict with least-cost routes that ignore local population); show results robust to dropping counties whose railroad precedes 1850.

────────────────────────────────────────
5. R CODE OUTLINE
────────────────────────────────────────
```r
#--------------------------------------------------
# 0. Packages
#--------------------------------------------------
library(data.table); library(sf); library(fixest); library(ivreg); library(did); 

#--------------------------------------------------
# 1. Load data
#--------------------------------------------------
county <- fread("county_panel_1790_2000.csv")   # county-year panel
geo    <- fread("county_geography.csv")         # time-invariant county vars
rail   <- fread("rail_arrival.csv")             # first railroad year by county
locks  <- fread("lock_completion.csv")          # canal/lock year by county
lights <- fread("lights_2003.csv")              # nighttime lights
tract  <- fread("tract_2000.csv")               # tract-level 2000 population
portage<- fread("portage_points.csv")           # lat/lon of portage sites

#--------------------------------------------------
# 2. Variable construction
#--------------------------------------------------
# a) mark counties treated
port.sf   <- st_as_sf(portage, coords=c("lon","lat"), crs=4326)
county.sf <- st_read("counties_shapefile.shp")
port.buff <- st_buffer(port.sf, dist=5000)  # 5 km buffer

county.sf$Portage <- as.integer(lengths(st_intersects(county.sf, port.buff))>0)
county <- merge(county, county.sf[,c("GEOID","Portage")], by="GEOID")

# b) obsolescence year = min(rail, lock)
county_0 <- merge(county, rail, by="GEOID")
county_0 <- merge(county_0, locks, by="GEOID", all.x=TRUE)
county_0[,Obsolete:=pmin(RailYear, LockYear, na.rm=TRUE)]

# c) event-time dummies
eventdummies <- function(dt, time, event, window=50){
  for(k in -window:window){
    var <- paste0("e",k)
    dt[[var]] <- as.integer((dt[[time]] - dt[[event]])==k)
  }; dt
}
county_0 <- eventdummies(county_0, "Year", "Obsolete", 70)

#--------------------------------------------------
# 3. MAIN DID / event-study (TWFE)
#--------------------------------------------------
formula_es <- as.formula(paste(
  "lpop ~", 
  paste(paste0("Portage*e",(-70:70)), collapse=" + "),
  "+ factor(Year) + factor(GEOID) + ", 
  "elevation + climate + distance_coast"
))
est_es <- feols(formula_es, data=county_0, cluster="river_segment")
summary(est_es)

#--------------------------------------------------
# 4. IV persistence (cross-section)
#--------------------------------------------------
cross <- county_0[Year==2000]
cross <- merge(cross, county_0[Year==1790, .(GEOID, pop1790=Pop)], by="GEOID")
cross$lnPop2000 <- log1p(cross$Pop)
cross$lnPop1790 <- log1p(cross$pop1790)

ivmod <- ivreg(lnPop2000 ~ lnPop1790 + controls |
                           Portage + controls,
               data=cross)
summary(ivmod)

#--------------------------------------------------
# 5. Robustness: Drop hydro-power rich sites
#--------------------------------------------------
ivmod2 <- update(ivmod, subset = (WaterPower1885 < quantile(WaterPower1885,0.9)))
summary(ivmod2)
```

────────────────────────────────────────
6. EXPECTED RESULTS
────────────────────────────────────────
• DID: Portage counties grow faster than controls before 1850; growth gap shrinks afterward but the level difference persists.  Event-study coefficients β_k should be ≈ 0 up to k = -1, jump up at k = 0, then remain flat.  
• IV: Coefficient of predicted ln Pop_1790 on ln Pop_2000 between 0.6 and 1.1.  I expect ≈ 0.8, implying substantial but less-than-proportional persistence (some increasing-returns, some mean-reversion).

────────────────────────────────────────
7. VALIDITY CHECKLIST SELF-ASSESSMENT (DID)
────────────────────────────────────────
C1: No anticipatory effects? … 1  
C2: Parallel pre-trends? ….. 1 (to be verified)  
C3: No spillovers? ………… 0 (possible river-segment spillovers)  
C4: Stable composition? ….. 1 (harmonised boundaries)  
C5: Correct functional form? 1 (log population with FE; robustness with arcsin pop share)

TOTAL: 4 / 5

────────────────────────────────────────
